# locker_auth_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Sign a remote locker in to Google Drive with your own OAuth client and store the result in
1Password.

## Synopsis

```text
locker_auth_tool [options]
```

## Description

Runs `rclone authorize` with the client, checks the new token can list the locker
folder, then writes `client_id`, `client_secret`, `token` and `root_folder_id` to the
1Password field `locker_<name>_config` references. Other stored options are kept,
apart from a service account's. The client and token never reach a command line.

Creating the client, once, in the Google Cloud console:

1. Create a project and enable the Google Drive API.
2. On Google Auth Platform > Branding, set an app name, support email, home page and
   privacy policy URLs, and add their domain to the authorized domains. Leave the logo
   empty: a logo needs Google's verification.
3. On Audience, choose External and Publish app, so it is In production. A Testing
   app's refresh tokens expire after 7 days. The app needs no verification.
4. On Clients, create a Desktop app client and download its JSON for `--client_file`.

When signing in, choose Advanced > Go to your app (or Continue) on the "Google hasn't
verified this app" page.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-l, --locker_type <locker_type>` | Remote locker to sign in. Default: `Gdrive`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `--client_file <client_file>` | JSON file downloaded for a Desktop app OAuth client; without it the stored client is used. |
| `--folder_id <folder_id>` | Id or URL of the Drive folder the locker is kept in; without it the stored folder is used. |
| `--no_browser` | Print the sign-in link instead of opening a browser. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Sign the Gdrive locker in to a folder

```bash
locker_auth_tool --client_file ~/Downloads/client_secret.json --folder_id https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEf
```

### Sign in again with the stored client and folder, printing the link

```bash
locker_auth_tool --no_browser
```

## Notes

- `locker_<name>_config` must be a 1Password reference in JoyBox.ini, such as
  `op://Personal/JoyBox/UserData.Share/locker_gdrive_config`; a missing field is created.
- Nothing is stored when the sign-in fails or the token cannot list the folder. Delete the client
  file once it is stored.
- The 1Password item is written back whole, so it must not hold a passkey, which the edit would
  drop.
- If Google answers with an error page, open the link in a private window, or wait a few minutes
  after publishing the app.
